Rep. Al Green (D-TX) moved Monday to force a vote on articles of impeachment against President Trump, his latest effort to remove the president from office.   His resolution cites what it calls the "unjustified" killings by federal immigration officers of Renée Good, Alex Pretti, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, among other issues.   The resolution says President Trump is guilty of high crimes and misdemeanors for "failing to uphold his constitutionally mandated solemn presidential oath of office to 'preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States,' thereby demonstrating that he is a great threat to democracy."   Since the resolution is "privileged," the House will have to act on it in some way within two legislative days. House Republicans are expected to hold a vote on a motion to table the resolution.   Rep. Green, whose previous efforts to impeach President Trump failed, lost his Democratic primary runoff in Texas's 18th District to Rep.
